bullets: Green plants make their own food in their leaves, using light, water and carbon dioxide
slides.heading: Photosynthesis: how green plants make food
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we meet the parts of a green plant, watch the leaf make food by photosynthesis, then see respiration - the reverse process - and clear up a common mistake about plants and breathing.

bullets: Name the leaf, stem and roots and say what each part does
Explain photosynthesis: light, water and carbon dioxide become food and oxygen
Explain respiration as the reverse process, happening day and night
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to name the plant parts, give the photosynthesis recipe, and explain why plants respire all the time.

bullets: A pupil says a plant cannot breathe because it has no nose and its chest never moves
Has breathing really stopped, or is it happening in a way we cannot see?
slides.heading: Do plants breathe?
slides.notes: Pose the puzzle from scene s4 without the verdict first: ask for a show of hands on whether plants breathe, take two or three answers without judging them, and say scene s4 settles this exactly.

bullets: Photosynthesis makes food in the leaf: light plus water plus carbon dioxide become food and oxygen
Respiration breaks food down with oxygen to release energy, and it happens all the time
slides.heading: Two processes in a green plant
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: photosynthesis stores food, respiration releases energy from that food, and the two processes run in opposite directions.

bullets: The leaf catches light, the stem holds the plant up, and the roots drink in water from the soil
Water drops sink into the soil and reach the root tips below the ground
slides.heading: Parts of a green plant
slides.notes: Narrate each part as it appears in the animation: point to the leaf catching light, the stem holding the plant up, and the roots below the soil drinking in water at the root tips.

bullets: Light, water from the roots and carbon dioxide from the air all arrive at the leaf
The leaf turns them into food and releases oxygen into the air
slides.heading: Photosynthesis: plants make their own food
slides.notes: Follow each ingredient as it moves: the sunlight reaching the leaf, the water drops travelling up from the roots, and the carbon dioxide flowing in, then watch the food appear and the oxygen leave the leaf.

bullets: Food and oxygen are broken down inside the leaf to release energy
Carbon dioxide and water are made - the reverse of the photosynthesis recipe
slides.heading: Respiration: the reverse process
slides.notes: Follow the food and oxygen into the leaf, watch the energy sparks rise as the food is broken down, then point to the carbon dioxide and water leaving: exactly the opposite direction from scene s2.

bullets: Gases move in and out of the leaf in the day and at night as well
A plant respires all the time, even when photosynthesis has stopped for the night
slides.heading: A common mistake: plants do not breathe?
slides.notes: Hold the mistake up first - the idea that a plant never breathes - then cross it out and watch the gases move in and out of the leaf first in the day and then at night.

bullets: Start with the ingredients: light from the sun, water from the roots and carbon dioxide from the air
Each ingredient arrives at the leaf, and the products are food for the plant plus oxygen for the air
slides.heading: Worked example: follow the recipe in the leaf
slides.notes: Talk through scene s2 slowly and name each ingredient as it arrives at the leaf, then name the two products: food that stays for the plant and oxygen that leaves into the air.

bullets: Trace photosynthesis for a leaf in bright light: what goes in, and what comes out?
Explain to your partner what changes at night, when photosynthesis stops but respiration carries on
slides.heading: Your turn: trace both processes
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each process: press them to name the inputs and outputs for photosynthesis, and to keep respiration running through the night in their second answer.

bullets: On your own: name the three main parts of a green plant and the job of each part
Give the photosynthesis recipe in one sentence and explain why a plant respires at night too
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for all three plant parts with their jobs, one clear recipe sentence, and a reason that respiration continues day and night.
